claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr is a single-phase BCC solid solution.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high strength at room temperature and elevated temperatures, including near 1000 °C.
The proposed intervention is partial replacement of Hf by Al to form (Hf1−xAlx)MoTaTiZr with x approximately 0.1–0.2.
Replacing Hf with lighter Al will reduce the alloy density.
Hf has an atomic weight of approximately 178.5 g/mol.
Al has an atomic weight of approximately 26.98 g/mol.
The Al-substituted alloy will retain a single BCC solid-solution phase.
Al atoms are expected to remain in solid solution because of similar atomic-size mismatch.
Dissolved Al will provide minor solid-solution strengthening.
Similar atomic radii and solid-solution strengthening will help maintain BCC phase stability and mechanical properties at room and elevated temperatures.

Refractory high-entropy alloys commonly form BCC solid solutions and can exhibit elevated-temperature mechanical performance associated with lattice distortion and high-melting-point refractory elements.
The cited subtraction study included HfMoTaTiZr among the investigated alloys.
The density is predicted to decrease from approximately 10.21 g/cm³ to approximately 9.5 g/cm³.
The Al-substituted alloy is predicted to retain yield strength comparable to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr at room temperature and near 1000 °C.
The Al-substituted alloy is predicted to retain ductility comparable to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr at room temperature and near 1000 °C.
The proposed performance boundary covers quasi-static tensile and compressive loading at room temperature and approximately 1000 °C in as-cast and annealed or aged conditions.
Al addition may cause brittle intermetallic or secondary phases, particularly during high-temperature annealing.
Formation of significant secondary phases or substantial loss of yield strength or ductility relative to the x = 0 control would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The phrase '10–20 atomic percent replacement' can imply 10–20 at.% Al in the whole alloy, whereas x = 0.1–0.2 in (Hf1−xAlx)MoTaTiZr replaces only 10–20% of the Hf sublattice and therefore gives approximately 2–4 at.% Al overall.
